title: Node 24 LTS Drops Its Own Permissions
caption:
Every npm package you install can read /etc/passwd. That's just the default.

Node 24.20.0 LTS landed Aug 26 with --permission-audit. It runs every permission check and denies nothing, so you can watch what your deps actually touch before you lock anything down.

The bit I like is drop(). Read your config at boot, then revoke fs.read before the rest of your app loads. It's irreversible on purpose.

When did you last audit a dependency?

slides.headline:
Your deps can
read /etc/passwd.
slides.sub: Node runs every dependency with your full user permissions. 24.20.0 LTS, Aug 26, ships the way out.

slides.title: Audit denies nothing
slides.sub: Every permission check still runs. Nothing throws. Violations publish to diagnostics_channel instead.

slides.title: node:permission-model:*
items: fs — every file system read and write
wasi, addon, ffi — the native code paths

slides.headline:
Then flip it
to enforce.
slides.sub:
node --permission --allow-fs-read=./data app.js

Everything you didn't name throws ERR_ACCESS_DENIED.

slides.headline:
Boot, then
revoke.
slides.sub: Read your config while you still can, then drop it before the rest of your app loads.

slides.title: read this part twice
items: drop() is irreversible. There is no way back
Open fds, sockets, children and workers stay open
Only future access checks are affected
Granted with a wildcard? You can only drop the whole scope
